analysis:
The supplied units are documentation-only head text in docs/architecture/inference.md (lines ~3204-3998). The file_changes patch shows changes at head lines 453-473 (cluster onboarding stop semantics) and 3239-3242 and 3255-3286 (loop guard events and the Gemma 4 thought-exit continuation). The units I reviewed contain the loop-guard section and later reasoning, JSON, tool-call and MiMo sections. The onboarding stop text at lines 453-473 lies outside the supplied units, so I could not examine it.

The loop-guard description introduces a continuation for Gemma 4 after a loop is detected in a thought. It re-submits the prompt plus the generated tokens and `<channel|>` on the same bridge, keeping the same cache scope, sampling and stop strings. Security-relevant points I checked:
- Continuation requests keep the original cache scope (cacheSalt), so T-041 account scoping is not widened by the documented behavior. No new at-rest artifact is described; the "cancelled row donates no KV" statement means no extra SSD donation.
- The documented logs and engine-health events carry only model, model_type, period, span, token counts and ends_thought. They carry no prompt content, which is consistent with A-001 handling.
- The continuation is bounded: it is skipped under 256 tokens of budget, it is capped at 8,192 tokens, and the wait for slot release is limited to 5 s. Billing reports the original prompt plus the combined completion tokens. No unbounded resource use or free-inference path is described (ADV-002).
- DARKBLOOM_LOOP_GUARD and DARKBLOOM_LOOP_EXIT_THINKING are passed to the launchd daemon through `LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys`. These are local operator controls and only affect the provider's own output behavior. Within TB-003 the operator is already untrusted for output integrity (T-007).
- Only docs are changed. I could not verify the implementation (EngineV2Bridge+Events, MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.prepareCompletion) against the text.

I found no concrete security regression. Remaining open question: whether the Swift implementation matches the docs. In particular, the continuation must reuse the original request's cacheSalt and must preserve the E2E encryption of response chunks (T-008). That belongs to a source-level review of the code files.
